text: If you jumped into a hole straight through the Earth, you'd come out the other side in thirty-eight minutes.
The deepest hole we've ever actually dug is twelve kilometers.
That's about a tenth of one percent of the way through.
So let's cheat. One tunnel, pole to pole, with all the air pumped out. Jump!
Down through the crust, then almost three thousand kilometers of hot rock.
Weirdly, gravity gets stronger as you fall, all the way to the core.
Thirteen minutes in, you plunge into an ocean of liquid iron.
Near the center it's about six thousand degrees. As hot as the surface of the Sun.
At the center, you're doing over twenty-eight thousand kilometers an hour, and you weigh nothing at all.
Now gravity pulls you back. You slow down, and down, and down.
Thirty-eight minutes after you jumped, you stop, right at the far side.
Grab the edge. Miss it, and you fall all the way back. Forever.
Unless you leave the air in. Then drag holds you to about two hundred kilometers an hour.
After more than a day of falling, you'd end up floating at the center of the Earth. Weightless. Stuck.
